title: Petting Your Dog May Protect You from Future Stress
paragraphs: If you know that life is about to get more stressful, petting your dog might be the preparation you need to make it easier to manage.

A study published in Biological Psychology looked at how interacting with their pets affected dog owners' responses to stress. The research included 64 dog owners, who took their pets to the researchers' lab while they did a stress test.
During the stress test, the participants had their heart rate and brain activity monitored.

There were two parts to the stress test. In one, participants had to answer general knowledge questions with a short time limit. The other part was an arithmetic task, with participants being asked to count backward following a set pattern and pace.
To add extra stress, the participants were told they were being video recorded, and someone gave them negative feedback when they got things wrong.

Between doing the two parts of the stress test, the participants were given a five-minute break, during which they sat on a chair in a room with their dog. The dog was either free to move around the room and go to their owner, or kept on a short leash and out of reach.
Unsurprisingly, the general knowledge and arithmetic tests caused signs of physical stress among participants, including increased heart rates and brain activity linked with feeling tense.

And while you might expect that interacting with their dog would help participants calm down, the stress levels of participants who could pet their dog during the recovery period didn't drop any faster than those who couldn't reach their dogs.

But participants who could pet their dog did show lower levels of stress during the second part of the test. This suggests that physical contact with their pet had a buffering effect for the stress they were about to experience.
So if you've got a stressful day ahead, be sure to pet your dog now — not later!
